messages:
Noah: Heads up 1011 HarborLogistics wants a 1-day POC next Tue. Must show streaming for live shipment updates, structured JSON output (schema validated), and a demo of a tool call to fetch shipment details. They also returned security questionnaire asking about mTLS, KMS, and evidence for SOC2. Can SE confirm feasibility and give quick hosted vs dedicated cost guidance?
Hannah: All good. SDKs support streaming (SSE/websocket) + resume. For strict JSON we recommend function-style outputs or `response_mode: json` + a validation layer, because model outputs can deviate. Tool-calls are supported; SDK emits tool events separately so the app can synthesize final JSON.
Noah: They specifically want resumable streams (client disconnects happen in their warehouse network). Any sample for resume?
Ravi: We have resume tokens on the stream. Flow: initial request -> server returns stream with chunks + optional resume_token header. On reconnect client sends `x-resume-token`. Example (py):
```py
resp = session.get(stream_url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TK}"}, stream=True)
for line in resp.iter_lines():
    process(line)
# on reconnect: headers["x-resume-token"] = latest_token
```
Hannah: Note: if you need exactly-once semantics for downstream ingestion, wrap with idempotency keys and validate schema before commit.
Sasha: Trust notes: hosted uses our KMS; for Private we support customer-managed keys (BYOK). SOC2 summary available; full pack via trust@redwood.ai. mTLS: we can enable mutual TLS on the demo gateway but ops needs a small window to provision certs. Data residency: we support us-east-1, eu-west-1.
Noah: They asked about webhooks for tool-call results 101 can Redwood call back to their internal webhook?
Ravi: Our runtime needs reachable endpoints. Options: 1) customer exposes public webhook (TLS + optional basic auth), 2) use an SSH/reverse-tunnel relay we can support for POC, or 3) deliver tool results in-stream so no external callback. For POC recommend in-stream delivery or temporary public endpoint.
Noah: Great. Pricing? Short POC spike: 40 QPS peak, ~120 tokens avg, 6h demo. Quick hosted vs dedicated notes?
Hannah: Quick calc: tokens = 40 * 3600 * 6 * 120 ~= 103.7M tokens. Hosted is easiest for short runs 101 expect $150100 depending on model. Dedicated cheaper per-token at scale but needs monthly commit and setup. I'll draft a one-pager with numbers.
Noah: Any enterprise blockers to flag before we send SOW?
Ravi: Potential blockers: mTLS provisioning window, if they insist on on-prem deployment it's ~4-6 weeks lead time, webhook reachability (firewall/NAT), and SSO/SAML contract terms if they want RBAC tied to their IdP. Also IP allowlist + private cross-connect requests take ops lead time.
Sasha: Also call out data processing agreements for EU customers if they request cross-border restrictions. If they need per-tenant encryption with customer keys that'll push to Private and needs legal + infra coordination.
Hannah: Action items:
- Hannah -> 1-page cost estimate hosted vs dedicated + model options (ETA: today afternoon)
- Ravi -> sample repo with resume example and an in-stream tool-call handler (ETA: tomorrow AM)
- Sasha -> SOC2 summary + BYOK/KMS checklist + mTLS cert rotation template (ETA: EOD)
- Noah -> confirm date with Harbor and share network contact + webhook endpoint plan (ETA: EOD)
ops-bot: [info] capacity-reserve: tentative slot requested for 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC for "harbor-poc".
Noah: I'll also ask them to provide a sanitized test dataset (no PII) and preferred JSON schema for the shipment object.
Hannah: I'll include a small validation shim in the sample that rejects nonconforming JSON and logs parse errors so demo stays clean.
Ravi: Reminder: if they want resume + strict ordering ensure the client attaches sequence ids to events. We'll include a quick client snippet.
Noah: Thanks all. Moving to SOW prep and I'll include these blockers in the draft. :thumbsup:
